region: Tocco da Casauria · Pescara, Abruzzo, Italy
about: The Toro distillery stands in Tocco da Casauria, a hill town in Abruzzo’s Pescara valley, between the Maiella massif and Monte Morrone. Its story begins in 1817, when the pharmacist Beniamino Toro started making an herbal liqueur in his pharmacy: Centerba, “a hundred herbs,” gathered in the surrounding mountains and steeped in spirit of startling strength. Centerba Toro, still bottled at around 70% alcohol, became the emblem of the town, and the family company carries on today as Enrico Toro Distilleria Casauria, making liqueurs from old recipes.

Centuca grew out of a local habit. In Abruzzo, drinkers long mixed sambuca with Centerba Toro to soften the herbal liqueur’s fierce edge, and the distillery eventually bottled the pairing itself, as the name suggests: Centerba plus sambuca. Its base is anise, from star anise and anise seed, with aromatic mountain herbs. Toro uses traditional alembic distillation and cold filtration, and the finished liqueur is perfectly clear.

Expect star anise and licorice first, then light herbal accents and a little spice, with restrained sweetness and a smooth, almost silky texture. For many guests it will be a first taste of Abruzzo’s centerba tradition in a gentler form. Like sambuca, it is taken as a digestivo at the end of a meal: neat, over ice, or with an espresso alongside.
